title: Construction Trailer Field Office Rates: Per-Sq-Ft and Monthly Cleaning Costs for Site Trailers
seoTitle: Construction Trailer Field Office Rates: Per-Sq-Ft & Monthly Cleaning
metaDescription: Construction trailer field office rates run $90-$150 per visit for a 1,440 sq ft double-wide. See monthly math by trailer size, then run the calculator.
excerpt: Site trailers are small, but mud, boot traffic, and a single overworked restroom push their cleaning cost per square foot well above a normal suite. This guide shows how per-visit minimums, frequency multipliers, and restroom counts translate into realistic monthly budgets for single-wide, double-wide, and multi-trailer compounds.
quickAnswer: Most construction trailer field offices under 2,500 sq ft price at $0.12-$0.20 per sq ft per visit, but the $90-$135 per-visit minimum usually controls the bill for single-wides. A 1,440 sq ft double-wide cleaned twice weekly typically lands at $1,550-$2,600 per month before restroom and consumable add-ons, while a 4,000 sq ft multi-trailer compound cleaned five nights a week runs roughly $7,400-$12,300 per month.

blocks.text: Why Site Trailers Cost More Per Square Foot Than a Normal Office

A general contractor's field office looks like an easy account on paper: 400 to 1,500 sq ft, a plan table, a few desks, a conference corner for OAC meetings, and one or two restrooms. In practice the trailer absorbs more soil per square foot than almost any Class B office. Every superintendent, foreman, inspector, and sub walks in straight from the laydown yard. Clay, gravel fines, concrete slurry, and drywall dust ride in on boots and settle into VCT seams, rubber transition strips, and the carpet tiles under the plan table. A crew that would clear 3,500 sq ft per hour in a standard suite (the ISSA production benchmark) often manages only 1,800 to 2,400 sq ft per hour in a busy trailer because the floor needs two passes and the entry needs scraping before mopping.

The second cost driver is the per-visit minimum. Vendors in most US metros will not dispatch a vehicle, a technician, and a cart of chemicals for less than $90 to $135 per stop. A 400 sq ft single-wide at $0.20 per sq ft calculates to only $80, so the minimum overrides the square-foot math. That is why small trailers look expensive on a per-sq-ft basis and why consolidating trailers on one compound into a single route stop saves real money.

The table below applies the national under-2,500 sq ft bracket ($0.12-$0.20 per sq ft per visit) and the 2,500-9,999 sq ft bracket ($0.09-$0.15) with the standard frequency multipliers and a VCT/vinyl floor factor of 1.04 or a mixed-floor factor of 1.05. Monthly totals use 4.33 weeks per month. Restroom servicing is shown separately because trailer restroom counts vary so widely.

blocks.title: Restroom density changes the math
blocks.text: Trailer restrooms are tiny but used by far more people than the desk count suggests, because field staff and visiting subs use them too. Budget $15-$30 per restroom per visit. A double-wide with two restrooms cleaned twice weekly adds $260-$520 per month (2 x $15-$30 x 8.66 visits). If the site also relies on portable toilets, confirm those are serviced by the sanitation rental company and excluded from janitorial scope.
Traffic Wear and Flooring: What Pushes a Trailer Toward the Top of the Range

Most modular field offices ship with VCT or sheet vinyl in the main area and low-pile carpet tiles in private offices. Vinyl is easier to recover from mud, but it scuffs under steel-toe boots and dulls quickly without periodic buffing. The quarterly deep floor program, amortized at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month, is worth adding to any trailer that will stand longer than six months. On a 1,440 sq ft double-wide that adds $43-$86 per month and prevents the scrub-and-recoat emergency that otherwise happens right before an owner walkthrough.

items: Entry scraping: trailers without a covered landing and exterior scraper mat generate up to twice the floor labor; a mat is cheaper than an extra mop pass every night.
Earthwork and foundation phases: expect peak soil load and price the top of the range during excavation, then renegotiate once the site is paved or in interior finishes.
Winter and rainy seasons: ice melt and wet clay create slip hazards on vinyl ramps and floors, which may justify a temporary frequency bump.
Plan rooms and conference corners: rolled drawings and plotter output create paper dust and heavy trash volumes that add bagging time.
Breakroom use: coffee stations and microwave lunches for 10-20 field staff justify the $12-$25 per-visit breakroom add-on.

blocks.text: Recommended Weekly Frequency by Project Phase

Frequency should follow the headcount and phase of the job, not the size of the trailer. A small residential project with a superintendent and assistant can get by with weekly service. A commercial job with an owner's rep, a project engineer, safety manager, and daily foremen meetings needs at least twice-weekly service, and large projects with a staffed compound and daily OAC or safety huddles usually justify five nights. Frequency multipliers work in your favor as you add visits: weekly service carries a 1.08 multiplier, twice weekly 1.00, three times 0.95, and daily weekdays 0.90, so the per-visit price drops as volume rises.

items.name: Count real daily occupants
items.text: Include field staff who use the restroom and breakroom, not just people with assigned desks. Over 15 daily users typically means 3x/week or more.

items.name: Map the project phase
items.text: Price the highest-soil phase first and write a frequency step-down clause for interior finish and closeout phases.

items.name: Separate restroom pricing
items.text: Ask bidders to list restroom servicing per visit so you can add or drop units as trailers are added or demobilized.

items.name: Decide on consumables
items.text: Vendor-supplied paper and soap runs $0.012-$0.025 per sq ft per visit; on small trailers it is often cheaper to stock your own through the GC's purchasing account.

items.name: Lock in mobilization terms
items.text: Specify how much notice is needed when trailers relocate on site or the project demobilizes, so you are not paying for a 30-day termination window after closeout.

blocks.text: Dispensers and Supplies That Lower Trailer Restock Labor

Restocking a trailer restroom is a hidden labor cost because cramped layouts make every refill slow. A Tork Elevation Matic H1 hand towel roll dispenser holds a 1,000-ft roll, feeds one towel at a time, locks with a key, and meets ADA reach requirements, which cuts both waste and mid-week run-outs. A San Jamar Classic Oceans twin 9-inch jumbo tissue dispenser holds two rolls on a universal core with a translucent cover, so the technician can see levels at a glance without opening it. A GOJO TFX touch-free foam soap dispenser takes a 1,200 mL refill rated for 2,000+ handwashes and keeps an ADA-compliant depth in narrow trailer restrooms. Together they let a weekly or twice-weekly crew stretch supplies between visits without callbacks from the superintendent.

blocks.title: Ask for a compound rate
blocks.text: If a project has a GC trailer, an owner's trailer, and a subcontractor break trailer, request one combined compound price. Treating three units as one stop eliminates two per-visit minimums and can cut 15-25% from the combined monthly invoice.
How to Read a Trailer Cleaning Bid

Line up each bid as per-visit labor, restroom count, add-ons, and consumables. Watch for vendors who quote a flat monthly price without specifying visits, because a slipped schedule during a rain week effectively raises your per-visit cost. Confirm the vendor carries general liability and workers' compensation that satisfy the GC's site requirements, that technicians will follow site-specific orientation and PPE rules, and that the crew knows where hazardous materials are stored so they do not empty a container of solvent rags into regular trash. Exclusions to look for include exterior steps and ramps, window exteriors, and portable toilet servicing.

Plug your trailer square footage, restroom count, and project-phase frequency into the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator, then paste competing vendor bids into the Quote Comparator to see whose per-visit math actually holds up.

faqs.q: Why does my 500 sq ft trailer cost almost as much as a 1,200 sq ft one?
faqs.a: Because the vendor's per-visit minimum, usually $90-$135, exceeds the square-foot calculation for small trailers. At $0.12-$0.20 per sq ft, a 500 sq ft unit calculates to only $60-$100 per visit, so the minimum takes over. Adding a second trailer to the same stop or bundling restroom service is the main way to get more value out of that minimum.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the monthly cost of twice-weekly trailer cleaning?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-visit price by 8.66 visits per month (2 visits x 4.33 weeks). A double-wide priced at $180-$300 per visit costs $1,556-$2,594 per month. Add restroom servicing at $15-$30 per restroom per visit and any breakroom or consumables add-ons on the same 8.66 multiplier.

faqs.q: What insurance should a trailer cleaning vendor provide?
faqs.a: Request a certificate of insurance showing commercial general liability (commonly $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate), workers' compensation at statutory limits, and auto liability for the service vehicle. Most GCs also require the owner and the GC to be named as additional insureds and a waiver of subrogation, so send your project insurance requirements with the bid request.

faqs.q: Does the cleaning crew need OSHA training to work on a construction site?
faqs.a: The crew is generally cleaning an office, not performing construction work, but the site's safety plan usually still applies. Expect them to attend site orientation, wear required PPE between the parking area and the trailer, and receive HazCom information about chemicals they bring on site through safety data sheets. Restroom work involving blood or bodily fluids falls under the vendor's bloodborne pathogens program.

faqs.q: Should I pay for quarterly floor care in a temporary trailer?
faqs.a: If the trailer will be on site longer than six months, yes. The amortized deep floor program at $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month costs only $43-$86 monthly on a 1,440 sq ft double-wide and keeps VCT presentable for owner meetings. For projects under six months, a single scrub before turnover to the leasing company may be enough and can help protect your damage deposit.
